title: ArtifactLifecycle
description:
The legal statuses and status transitions for one artifact kind.

Lifecycles differ by kind — an ADR goes `proposed → accepted → superseded`, a design goes `draft → in_review → approved → implemented` — and validation rejects a status a kind does not have, which catches the copy-paste error that would otherwise make a requirement silently unsatisfiable.

A document that names **no** kind is the tree's fallback: the lifecycle every kind with no nearer one is held to, and the only way to make a rule bind kinds nobody has enumerated. One tree may declare at most one. A lifecycle registered for the kind itself, or for a kind it specialises, always wins over it.

initial.description: The status a new artifact starts in.

kind.description: The kind this lifecycle governs; absent for the fallback lifecycle.

transitions.description: For each status, the statuses it may move to.

ArtifactKind.description: Artifact kind in kebab-case; the named vocabulary is listed in `examples`, and any other kebab-case name is accepted as an organisation-specific kind.

ArtifactStatus.description: Artifact status. The named vocabulary is listed in `examples`; any other name a lifecycle document declares is carried verbatim, so a rung is a line in a YAML file rather than a release of the engine.
